reasons: Your own app costs a Marketplace review. Until Zoom approves it, only users on your own Zoom account can connect: anyone outside it gets 'This app cannot be installed outside of the developer's account.' Composio's managed app lets you skip that review entirely, so stay on it until you have a reason to switch.
Your users see the name and logo of whichever app they authorize on Zoom's consent screen. On the managed app that is Composio's app, not your product.

You control the scopes. Composio's default scope list includes admin scopes (report:read:admin, device:read:admin, meeting:read:admin and others), and Zoom only lets a user with the matching account-level permissions authorize those. With your own app you can request user-level scopes only, so ordinary users can connect. Zoom reviewers also reject apps that request scopes they do not use.

Rate limits are not a reason to switch. Zoom applies them to the account the call is made for, shared across all apps installed on that account, so a shared managed app does not pool your users' quota with other developers' traffic.

verdict.summary: Reviewed. You can create a General app and connect accounts on your own Zoom account within an hour, but nobody outside that account can connect until Zoom's Marketplace team approves the app, even if you keep it unlisted. Zoom quotes 72 hours for the first review stage and up to 2 weeks for the security review; recent developer reports describe 2 to 4+ weeks. Composio's managed Zoom app avoids all of this, so use it until branding or scopes force your own.

timeToTesting.label: 20-45 min (users on your own Zoom account only)

timeToProduction.label: 1-6 weeks: Zoom states 72 hours plus up to 2 weeks of security review; 2025-2026 reports run longer. Add time to write the docs and test plan

verdict.mainBlocker: Zoom's Marketplace review (functional review, then a security review that checks your technical design documents and runs security tests). It is mandatory before any user outside your own Zoom account can connect, and unlisted apps get the same review.

stages.name: Register the app
limits: Choose user-managed or admin-managed when you create the app. Admin-managed apps are added by account admins and can reach other users' data on that account; user-managed apps only reach the authorizing user's own data.
Apps created since about March 2024 only offer Zoom's granular scopes. Composio's published default list uses the older classic scope names, so you have to pick the matching granular scopes yourself.

steps.title: Create a General app
steps.detail: In the Zoom App Marketplace, choose Develop, then Build App, then General App. Pick user-managed if each user connects their own Zoom, or admin-managed if an account admin connects the whole account. Name it after your product: this is what users see when they authorize. Composio's credentials guide also mentions server-to-server apps, but those are for a single account and have no user redirect flow; use a General app for Composio's OAuth2 connections.
steps.humanReason: Requires signing in to your Zoom account in the Marketplace.

steps.title: Set the redirect URL and allow list
steps.detail: Under OAuth Information, paste Composio's redirect URI into Redirect URL and add the same URL to the OAuth Allow List. Copy it from your Composio dashboard when you create the Zoom auth config. Composio's Zoom credentials page shows a /api/v3/ callback path, while Composio's knowledge base warns against reusing legacy v1 or v3 callback paths, so trust the dashboard over either page.
steps.humanReason: Inside your signed-in Zoom developer console.

preparedValues.label: Redirect URL and OAuth Allow List entry
preparedValues.value: Copy from Composio: Auth Configs > Create Auth Config > Zoom > OAuth2

steps.title: Add scopes
steps.detail: Open Scopes and add only the granular scopes for the Composio Zoom tools your agent uses. Prefer user-level scopes over :admin scopes unless an admin will authorize. Reviewers reject unused or overlapping scopes and want a justification for each one, so keep the list short from the start.

links.label: Migrate from classic to granular scopes

preparedValues.label: Composio's default classic scopes (map each to its granular equivalent)
preparedValues.value: meeting:read meeting:write recording:read recording:write webinar:read webinar:write:registrant

steps.title: Copy the development Client ID and Secret
steps.detail: Under App Credentials, copy the development Client ID and Client Secret for testing. Zoom also issues production credentials, which you use once the app is published. Treat each secret like a password: it goes into Composio and nowhere else.
steps.humanReason: The secret should only pass from your console to Composio.

stages.name: Connect it in Composio and test
limits: Before review, only members of your own Zoom account can authorize the app.
Access tokens last 1 hour. Refresh tokens expire after 90 days, and each refresh should use the latest refresh token.
Apps in development do not send deauthorization notifications, so you cannot test that flow until the app is published.

steps.title: Create the Zoom auth config in Composio
steps.detail: Create an OAuth2 auth config for Zoom with your development Client ID, Client Secret and the same scopes you added in Zoom. Composio states Zoom has no bearer token option, so use OAuth2.

steps.title: Connect a user on your own Zoom account
steps.detail: Start a connection, approve the consent screen with a user on the same Zoom account that owns the app, and run one read tool (for example, list meetings). Use an admin user if you added any :admin scopes. A user from any other Zoom account will be refused until the app is published.
steps.humanReason: You approve the consent screen with your own Zoom account.

stages.name: Get the app reviewed and published

duration.label: Zoom: 72 hours plus up to 2 weeks. Reported: 5 business days to 4+ weeks

limits: Review is required for public and unlisted apps alike. Only private apps (your own account) skip it.
Terms of Use, Privacy Policy, support and documentation pages must be on a domain your company owns. Google Drive or Dropbox links are rejected.
Rate limits follow each customer's Zoom plan, from 4 requests per second (Free, light APIs) to 80 (Business and up), and each user can create or update at most 100 meetings per day.

steps.title: Prepare the listing pages
steps.detail: Publish a Terms of Use, Privacy Policy, Support page (with support hours, response time and contact methods) and user documentation on your own domain. The documentation needs sections on adding the app, using it, removing it (including what happens to the data) and troubleshooting. Unlisted apps still need images, a description and categories, because Zoom shows them on the user's added-apps page.

steps.title: Handle deauthorization
steps.detail: When a user removes the app, you must handle Zoom's deauthorization event notification and revoke their tokens, or rely on Zoom's standard removal process. Check with Composio how its connections react to a Zoom deauthorization event before you submit.

steps.title: Write the test plan and test accounts
steps.detail: Give reviewers a step-by-step test plan covering every scope you request, plus login credentials for test accounts with sample data (two accounts if a flow needs them). A recorded walkthrough, for example a Loom link, is optional but recommended by developers who have been through review.

steps.title: Submit for review
steps.detail: Submit the app with its technical design documentation and the security and privacy answers. Choose unlisted if you only want your own users to install it through your link; the review is the same. Zoom first checks completeness, branding and functionality, then its security team audits the app, including OWASP Top 10 testing. You can submit from a free Zoom account. Watch the developer contact email: Zoom sends review findings there.
steps.humanReason: A submission and legal agreement (Marketplace Developer Agreement) made on behalf of your company.

steps.title: Switch Composio to production credentials
steps.detail: Once the app is approved, put the production Client ID and Secret into your Composio auth config. Zoom says to use production credentials once the app is published.

requirements.title: Marketplace review before any outside user
requirements.detail: Users outside your Zoom account can only install the app after it passes Zoom's review. Unlisted apps are reviewed the same way and must meet the same security and privacy requirements.

requirements.title: Terms of Use, Privacy Policy, documentation and support URL on your own domain
requirements.detail: Required by the Marketplace Developer Agreement. Pages on third-party hosts are a common rejection reason.

requirements.title: Test plan and test credentials
requirements.detail: Reviewers need a plan covering every scope and working test logins. An insufficient test plan is the first rejection reason Zoom lists.

requirements.title: Minimum scopes, each justified
requirements.detail: Request only the scopes your tools use; reviewers reject unused or overlapping scopes. New apps use granular scopes.

requirements.title: Deauthorization handling
requirements.detail: Removing the app must revoke tokens and handle the deauthorization event, or use Zoom's standard removal.

requirements.title: Tokens expire: 1 hour access, 90 days refresh
requirements.detail: Always use the latest refresh token. A user whose refresh token expires has to reconnect.

requirements.title: No fee
requirements.detail: Zoom staff say a paid plan is not needed to create or submit Marketplace apps, though some features (webinars, Zoom Phone) need a license to test.

blockers.title: Users outside your account cannot connect
blockers.symptom: The consent screen says 'This app cannot be installed outside of the developer's account. Please contact the application developer to get support with installing this application.'
blockers.fix: Expected until Zoom approves the app. Test with users on your own Zoom account, or keep using Composio's managed Zoom app until your own app is published.

blockers.title: Redirect URL mismatch
blockers.symptom: Zoom shows a redirect or invalid redirect_uri error before the user can approve.
blockers.fix: Make the Redirect URL and the OAuth Allow List entry identical to the redirect URI in your Composio auth config. Copy it from the Composio dashboard; if it changed, recreate or update the auth config.

blockers.title: Scopes from Composio's guide are not in the scope picker
blockers.symptom: You search for meeting:read or recording:read:admin and cannot find them in a newly created app.
blockers.fix: New apps only list granular scopes. Pick the granular scopes that cover the same APIs. Tools that fail with a scope error need the missing scope added to your app and to the Composio auth config, then a reconnect.

blockers.title: Ordinary users cannot authorize admin scopes
blockers.symptom: Non-admin users fail at consent, or admin tools return permission errors.
blockers.fix: Apps with :admin scopes must be authorized by a user with the matching account-level permissions. Drop the admin scopes or have an admin connect.

blockers.title: Customer account requires pre-approval
blockers.symptom: Users see 'Request pre-approve' instead of being able to install.
blockers.fix: The customer's Zoom Marketplace admin must pre-approve your app (Marketplace > Manage > Permissions), or turn off the pre-approval requirement.

blockers.title: Review rejected
blockers.symptom: Zoom returns the submission with findings to fix.
blockers.fix: The listed causes are a weak test plan, the wrong Client ID, pages hosted on third-party domains, missing documentation sections, unused or overlapping scopes, missing deauthorization handling, thin support information and missing listing metadata. Fix and resubmit.

blockers.title: 429 errors for one customer
blockers.symptom: Calls fail with HTTP 429 for one customer account.
blockers.fix: That account's plan limit is used up, and it is shared with every other app installed on the account. Back off and retry; meeting create or update calls are also capped at 100 per user per day.

agentCan: Map the Composio Zoom tools you use to the smallest set of granular scopes, preferring user-level over admin scopes
Prepare every value to paste into the Zoom developer console
Create the Composio auth config through Composio's API once you give it the Client ID and Secret through a secure channel
Draft the Terms of Use, Privacy Policy, support page and user documentation sections Zoom requires
Write the test plan, with one section per scope, and the scope justifications
Implement deauthorization handling if your backend needs it
youMust: Sign in to the Zoom App Marketplace and create the app
Approve the first consent screen with a user on your own Zoom account
Host the legal and support pages on your company's domain
Accept the Marketplace Developer Agreement and submit the app for review
Create and populate test accounts for the reviewers, and answer their findings

unknowns.whyItMatters: If it is not published, users outside Composio's own Zoom account could not connect through it, and the managed option would only work for testing.

unknowns.question: Which granular scopes match Composio's default classic scope list?
unknowns.whyItMatters: New Zoom apps cannot select classic scopes, and Composio's credentials guide only lists classic names.
unknowns.draftEmail: Hi Composio team, your Zoom credentials guide lists classic scopes such as meeting:read and recording:read:admin, but new Zoom General apps only offer granular scopes. Do you have a list of granular scopes per Zoom tool, and does the toolkit work with an app that uses granular scopes only? Thanks.

unknowns.question: Can Composio's Zoom toolkit use a server-to-server app?
unknowns.whyItMatters: Composio's guide says to create a General or server-to-server app; server-to-server apps are internal to one account and would avoid review for internal use.
unknowns.draftEmail: Hi Composio team, your Zoom credentials guide mentions creating a General or server-to-server app. Does the Zoom toolkit support server-to-server OAuth (account credentials), and if so, how is it configured in an auth config? Thanks.

unknowns.question: Do connections made with development credentials keep working after publication, or must every user reconnect on production credentials?
unknowns.whyItMatters: Decides whether your test users have to reconnect when you switch the auth config to production credentials.

unknowns.whyItMatters: Zoom's own pages disagree: one limits beta apps to the developer's account, another allows external sharing after Zoom approves it. If the second holds, you can pilot with a customer while the full review runs.

Which is current, what documentation do you need, and how long does that approval usually take? Thanks.
